CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]

SPECIMEN INFORMATION
Specimen Type: Amniotic fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]
Gestational Age at Collection: 15 weeks

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal testing for chromosomal abnormalities
Screening for Down syndrome and other aneuploidies

TEST PERFORMED
Conventional Cytogenetic Analysis - G-banded Karyotype

METHODOLOGY
Amniotic fluid cells were cultured according to standard protocols. Metaphase chromosomes were harvested and G-banded using trypsin-Giemsa staining. A minimum of 20 metaphase cells were analyzed at the 400-550 band resolution level. Five cells were fully karyotyped and documented.

RESULTS
Karyotype: 46,XX

INTERPRETATION
Normal female chromosomal complement identified. No evidence of trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) or other numerical or structural chromosomal abnormalities detected in the cells analyzed. All chromosomes appear normal in number and structure at the resolution of this analysis.

Cells Analyzed: 20
Cells Karyotyped: 5
Band Resolution: 400-550

CLINICAL CORRELATION
This result indicates a chromosomally normal female fetus. The normal karyotype excludes common chromosomal causes of intellectual disability and birth defects detectable by conventional cytogenetic analysis, including:
- Trisomy 21 (Down syndrome)
- Trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome)
- Trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome)
- Sex chromosome aneuploidies
- Large structural rearrangements

LIMITATIONS
G-banded karyotype analysis cannot detect:
- Microdeletions or microduplications smaller than 5-10 Mb
- Single gene disorders
- Low-level mosaicism (<10%)
- Uniparental disomy
- Methylation abnormalities

RECOMMENDATIONS
This result supersedes any previous rapid aneuploidy screening results (e.g., QF-PCR, FISH) performed on this pregnancy. No additional cytogenetic testing is indicated based on these findings. Continue routine prenatal care as recommended by the referring physician.

For detection of submicroscopic chromosomal abnormalities or single gene disorders, chromosomal microarray analysis or other molecular genetic testing may be considered if clinically indicated.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Cytogenetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA. The FDA has determined that such clearance or approval is not necessary.
